questions.question: At which World Cup were the players' shirt numbers permanently fixed to a squad list for the first time?
questions.fun_fact: Before 1954, numbers were often handed out match by match, so a player could wear different numbers in different games — and goalkeepers didn't even reliably wear number 1.

questions.question: The very first World Cup in 1930 had no qualifying tournament. How did teams get in?
questions.fun_fact: FIFA invited everyone, but the long boat trip to Uruguay scared off most of Europe — only four European teams made the crossing, and France's squad shared the voyage with Brazil and Romania.

questions.question: Which country has hosted the men's World Cup despite never qualifying for one on the pitch beforehand?
questions.fun_fact: Qatar's 2022 appearance was its tournament debut, granted automatically as host — and the team lost all three group games, the first host ever eliminated after just two matches.

questions.question: In 1950, the World Cup was decided without a single official final match. How was the winner determined instead?
questions.fun_fact: The decisive game between Uruguay and Brazil happened to be the last group fixture, so the 'Maracanazo' felt like a final — but technically the trophy was won on points, not in a knockout.

questions.question: At the 1982 World Cup, a notorious match led FIFA to change a scheduling rule forever. What was the fix?

answers.text: Final group games kick off simultaneously
Group winners are seeded by lottery
Draws were banned in group play

questions.fun_fact: After West Germany and Austria played out a result that conveniently knocked Algeria out, FIFA mandated that the last two group matches start at the same time so neither side knows what result it needs.

questions.question: Why did the 1930 World Cup final use two different match balls — one per half?

answers.text: Each finalist insisted on its own ball
The first ball burst at halftime

questions.fun_fact: Argentina supplied the ball for the first half and led 2-1; Uruguay used theirs in the second half and won 4-2 — fueling a long-running joke about whose ball was 'luckier.'

questions.question: Which World Cup was the first to be broadcast live on television?
questions.fun_fact: The 1954 broadcast reached only a handful of European countries with TV sets, but it set the template — by 1970 the World Cup was beamed in color and across continents via satellite.

questions.question: Mexico 1970 introduced an innovation now standard in every sport. What was it?
questions.fun_fact: A referee dreamed up the color-card idea after a language mix-up in 1966 — he reportedly got the inspiration from traffic lights while driving home.

questions.question: Substitutions as we know them were not allowed at the World Cup until surprisingly late. At which tournament were tactical substitutions first generally permitted?
questions.fun_fact: Before 1970, an injured player simply left his team a man down for the rest of the match — even goalkeepers who got hurt had to be replaced by an outfield teammate in the gloves.

questions.question: The 1938 World Cup featured a defending champion that didn't have to qualify but also barely existed as a unit. Which oddity occurred?

answers.text: Defending champ Italy got an automatic spot for the first time
Two host nations shared the tournament
The trophy was sent by mail to the winner

questions.fun_fact: 1938 was the first time the reigning champion (and the host) earned automatic qualification — a privilege champions kept until 2006, when titleholders had to qualify again.

questions.question: What unusual thing happened to the original World Cup trophy in 1966, months before the tournament?

answers.text: It was stolen and found by a dog
It was melted down by mistake
It sank with a cargo ship

questions.fun_fact: The Jules Rimet trophy vanished from a London exhibition, then a dog named Pickles sniffed it out wrapped in newspaper under a hedge — the pup became a national celebrity.

questions.question: The 1986 World Cup in Mexico had a strange backstory: it was originally awarded to a different country. Which one pulled out?
questions.fun_fact: Colombia withdrew citing economic strain, and Mexico stepped in — becoming the first nation to host the men's World Cup twice, despite a major earthquake striking months before kickoff.

questions.question: At the 1994 World Cup, FIFA changed how many points a win was worth. What was the change?
questions.fun_fact: The three-points-for-a-win rule was meant to reward attacking play and discourage cagey draws — it worked so well it's now universal across world football.

questions.question: Which World Cup was the first held entirely in two co-hosting countries?
questions.fun_fact: The two co-hosts couldn't even agree on the official name order, so FIFA settled it alphabetically — which is why it's 'Korea/Japan' and not 'Japan/Korea.'

questions.question: Penalty shootouts didn't always exist at the World Cup. How were drawn knockout games settled before they were introduced?

answers.text: By replaying the match or drawing lots

questions.fun_fact: Italy reached the 1968 European final by a literal coin toss, which embarrassed officials into adopting shootouts — the World Cup's first one came in 1982.

questions.question: The 1974 World Cup introduced a second, smaller trophy because of a permanent decision about the first. What was it?

answers.text: Brazil kept the old trophy forever after three wins
The old trophy was retired due to damage
FIFA banned gold trophies for cost reasons

questions.fun_fact: Jules Rimet had decreed any nation winning three times would keep the cup outright; Brazil did so in 1970, prompting the brand-new FIFA World Cup Trophy that's still used today.

questions.question: At the 1938 World Cup, one nation reached the quarterfinals without playing a single match. How?

answers.text: Their opponent withdrew before the game
They were given a bye by lottery

questions.fun_fact: Sweden advanced when Austria withdrew after being annexed by Germany — its players were absorbed into the German squad, an early case of politics reshaping the bracket.

questions.question: Goalkeepers gained a famous restriction at the 1994 World Cup era. What were they newly banned from doing?
questions.fun_fact: The back-pass rule was rushed in after the 1990 tournament was criticized as too defensive, with keepers killing time by holding the ball — it forced a faster, more open game.

questions.question: The first World Cup mascot appeared in 1966. What was it?

answers.text: A lion named World Cup Willie

questions.fun_fact: World Cup Willie kicked off the entire tradition of tournament mascots and even got his own pop song — every cartoon mascot since traces back to that English lion.

questions.question: Which World Cup first expanded the field from 16 to 24 teams?
questions.fun_fact: The jump from 16 to 24 teams in 1982 opened the door for debutants from Africa, Asia and beyond — Algeria and Cameroon both stunned European giants that year.

questions.question: Which player scored the only goal of the 2014 World Cup final, coming off the bench to do it?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first World Cup final ever decided by a substitute's goal, and it made Germany the first European team to win the tournament on South American soil.

questions.question: Who scored the first hat-trick in a men's World Cup final?
questions.fun_fact: Hurst did it in 1966, and it took 56 years for anyone to match him: Kylian Mbappé scored three in the 2022 final and still finished a runner-up.

questions.question: Which player was sent off in a World Cup final for a headbutt to the chest?
questions.fun_fact: Zidane was voted the tournament's best player and collected the Golden Ball award even though his last act on a pitch was that red card in the 2006 final.

questions.question: Mexican goalkeeper Antonio Carbajal was the first man to do what at the World Cup?

answers.text: Save three penalties in one match

questions.fun_fact: Carbajal appeared at five World Cups between 1950 and 1966; it took until 1998 for Lothar Matthäus to become the second man to reach five.

questions.question: Cristiano Ronaldo was the first male player to score at how many separate World Cup tournaments?
questions.fun_fact: He scored in 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022; Lionel Messi has since matched the feat of scoring at five different World Cups.

questions.question: Kylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick in the 2022 World Cup final and still lost. Which team beat his France?
questions.fun_fact: Argentina won the final on penalties, meaning Mbappé became the first man to score a final hat-trick and still end up a runner-up.

questions.question: Which player both lifted the World Cup as captain and later won it as a head coach?
questions.fun_fact: Beckenbauer captained West Germany to victory in 1974 and coached them to the title in 1990; only Mário Zagallo and Didier Deschamps have otherwise won as both player and coach.

questions.question: Who is the youngest player ever to score in a men's World Cup final?
questions.fun_fact: He scored twice in the 1958 final and, by his own account, fainted at the final whistle.

questions.question: Who is the only goalkeeper ever to win the Golden Ball as the best player of a World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Kahn won the 2002 award despite spilling a shot in the final that handed Brazil the opening goal in their 2-0 win — the only major error he made all tournament.

questions.question: Who holds the record for the most goals scored in a single World Cup tournament?
questions.fun_fact: Fontaine scored 13 in 1958 — and according to legend played the tournament in borrowed boots after his own pair fell apart beforehand.

questions.question: Who scored the fastest goal in World Cup history?
questions.fun_fact: Turkey's Şükür scored against South Korea in 2002, in the third-place play-off. It was the only goal he scored all tournament.

questions.question: Which striker scored five goals in a single World Cup match, the most ever in one game?
questions.fun_fact: Russia's Salenko hit five against Cameroon in 1994, yet Russia were knocked out in the group stage and he never played another World Cup match.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 1962 World Cup, two years after the strongest earthquake ever recorded?
questions.fun_fact: The Valdivia earthquake of 1960 had destroyed much of the country, and stadiums were rebuilt against the clock to keep the tournament.

questions.question: Which player won the World Cup as a player and then won it again as the head coach of the same nation?
questions.fun_fact: Zagallo won as a Brazil player in 1958 and 1962 and as coach in 1970; he was also a backroom figure in the 1994 win, giving him four titles in different roles.

questions.question: At the 1990 World Cup, Cameroon's Roger Milla famously celebrated his goals by doing what at the corner flag?
questions.fun_fact: Milla was 38 in 1990 and came out of international retirement after a personal phone call from Cameroon's president; four years later he became the oldest goalscorer in World Cup history.

questions.question: Jairzinho achieved a feat at the 1970 World Cup that no other player has matched in a title-winning run. What was it?

answers.text: He scored in every match of the tournament
He saved a penalty as an outfield player
He played all 90 minutes without touching the ball

questions.fun_fact: Jairzinho scored in all six of Brazil's games in 1970, including the final — no other player has scored in every match of a World Cup they went on to win.

questions.question: Which Dutch defender scored an own goal AND a normal goal in the same 1978 World Cup match?
questions.fun_fact: Brandts put through his own net against Italy, then equalised at the correct end in the same game; the Netherlands won and reached the final.

questions.question: Which player scored in two different World Cup finals, eight years apart?
questions.fun_fact: Breitner converted a penalty in West Germany's 1974 final win and scored again in the 1982 final loss — one of only three men to score in two separate finals, alongside Pelé and Vavá.

questions.question: Which stadium has hosted two World Cup finals?
questions.fun_fact: 1970 and 1986, both in Mexico City. The Maracanã has hosted one final, in 2014; the deciding match of 1950 was not officially one.

questions.question: Which player scored the very first goal in World Cup history at the 1930 tournament?
questions.fun_fact: Frenchman Laurent later said no film of his historic 1930 goal survives, and that it was bitterly cold during the match in Montevideo's Southern Hemisphere winter.

questions.question: Which team reached the 2014 quarter-finals without losing a match in normal time?
questions.fun_fact: It finished ahead of Uruguay, Italy and England in the group and went out to the Netherlands on penalties.

questions.question: In the 1950 World Cup, the United States stunned England in a famous upset. What was the score?
questions.fun_fact: The result was so improbable that some British newspapers reportedly assumed it was a typo and printed it as a 10–1 England win instead.

questions.question: At the 1986 World Cup, Diego Maradona scored two goals against England within four minutes that could not have been more different. What were they?

answers.text: An illegal handball, then a brilliant solo run

questions.fun_fact: Maradona later called the handball goal the "Hand of God," while the solo effort was voted Goal of the Century by FIFA voters.

questions.question: In the 1998 World Cup, France beat Saudi Arabia, but their star Zinedine Zidane was sent off for what?
questions.fun_fact: Zidane served a two-match ban but returned to score twice in the final against Brazil, both with his head.

questions.question: During a 2010 World Cup quarterfinal, Uruguay's Luis Suárez kept Ghana out of the semifinals by doing what on the goal line?

answers.text: Punching the ball away with his hands
Catching it like a goalkeeper for a throw
Heading it onto his own crossbar

questions.fun_fact: Suárez was sent off, but Ghana missed the resulting penalty and then lost the shootout — so his deliberate handball arguably worked.

questions.question: In a 1982 World Cup match, West Germany and Austria were accused of arranging a result that conveniently knocked Algeria out. What was the suspicious score?
questions.fun_fact: The "Disgrace of Gijón" led FIFA to make the final group matches kick off simultaneously at all future World Cups.

questions.question: Which country returned to the World Cup in 2018 after a 36-year absence?
questions.fun_fact: Its previous appearance had been at Spain 1982.

questions.question: In a 2006 World Cup match, referee Graham Poll showed the same Croatian player how many yellow cards before sending him off?
questions.fun_fact: Josip Šimunić's name was misheard as sounding Australian, contributing to Poll forgetting he'd already booked him; the referee never officiated at a World Cup again.

questions.question: Which team played the 1954 final after losing 8-3 to that same opponent in the group stage?
questions.fun_fact: It won the final 3-2 against a Hungary side unbeaten for four years. The game is remembered as the Miracle of Bern.

questions.question: In the 1990 World Cup, Cameroon shocked defending champions Argentina in the opening match while finishing the game with how many men?

answers.text: Nine men, after two red cards
Ten men, after one red card

questions.fun_fact: Cameroon won 1–0 despite the two dismissals, and 38-year-old Roger Milla's dancing celebrations later that tournament made him a global sensation.

questions.question: At the 1974 World Cup, Zaire's Mwepu Ilunga did something baffling at a free kick that confused everyone. What?

answers.text: He ran out and booted the ball away before it was taken
He sat down in the defensive wall
He picked the ball up and handed it to the referee

questions.fun_fact: Ilunga later said he understood the rules perfectly and was deliberately wasting time after the team had been threatened by their own dictator over results.

questions.question: In the 1970 World Cup, England's first-choice goalkeeper Gordon Banks famously missed the quarterfinal against West Germany because of what?
questions.fun_fact: England led 2–0 with deputy Peter Bonetti in goal but lost 3–2 in extra time; conspiracy theories about Banks's sudden illness persist to this day.

questions.question: At the 1994 World Cup, Colombia's Andrés Escobar scored an own goal against the USA that had a tragic aftermath. What happened to him?

answers.text: He was murdered days after returning home
He was banned from football for life
He retired immediately from the sport

questions.fun_fact: The own goal contributed to Colombia's shock elimination, and Escobar was shot in his home country shortly after the team flew back.

questions.question: In a 1938 World Cup quarterfinal between Brazil and Czechoslovakia, the match was so violent that how many players were sent off?

answers.text: None — it was a clean game

questions.fun_fact: The game became known as the "Battle of Bordeaux," and it left two Czechoslovak players with a broken arm and a broken leg.

questions.question: At the 2010 World Cup, the final between Spain and the Netherlands set a record for what?

answers.text: The most yellow cards in a World Cup final
The most goals in a World Cup final

questions.fun_fact: English referee Howard Webb handed out 14 cards, including a red, in a final famous for a Dutch player's flying kung-fu kick to a Spaniard's chest.

questions.question: In the 1982 World Cup semifinal, France led West Germany 3–1 in extra time but lost. How did the match end?

answers.text: On penalties, after West Germany clawed it back to 3–3
West Germany scored a last-minute fourth in extra time
France conceded after a disallowed goal of their own

questions.fun_fact: Earlier in the game German keeper Harald Schumacher flattened a French player so brutally the Frenchman lost teeth, yet no foul was given.

questions.question: At the 2018 World Cup, the final between France and Croatia featured which unusual first?

answers.text: The first own goal scored in a World Cup final
The first final decided by penalties

questions.fun_fact: The match also saw the first VAR-awarded penalty in a final, plus a pitch invasion by protesters during the second half.

questions.question: Which Colombian scored the goal that won the FIFA Puskás Award after the 2014 World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: A chest control with his back to goal and a volley from outside the box, against Uruguay.

questions.question: At the 1998 World Cup, England's David Beckham was sent off against Argentina for what?

answers.text: Flicking a petulant kick at an opponent while lying down
Arguing with the referee over a throw-in

questions.fun_fact: England lost on penalties, and Beckham was so vilified at home that one pub reportedly hung his effigy outside before he later rehabilitated his reputation.

questions.question: In the 1974 World Cup, the very first goal was scored from the penalty spot before which team had even touched the ball?

answers.text: West Germany conceded to the Netherlands

questions.fun_fact: The Dutch passed the ball among themselves 16 times straight from kickoff before being fouled in the box — no German player had touched it yet.

questions.question: Which host nation was eliminated in the group stage of its own World Cup in 2010?
questions.fun_fact: South Africa remains the only host nation ever to fail to reach the knockout rounds of a men's World Cup.

questions.question: Which country knocked defending champions Germany out in the 2018 group stage?
questions.fun_fact: It was Germany's earliest exit in 80 years, and South Korea didn't even advance themselves despite winning that match.

questions.question: Which team beat reigning champions France in the opening match of the 2002 World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Many of Senegal's players had grown up in France; France then went out in the group stage without scoring a single goal.

questions.question: Which reigning champion boycotted the very next World Cup, in 1934, in protest?
questions.fun_fact: Uruguay was angry that European nations had snubbed its 1930 tournament, and remains the only champion ever to skip defending its title.

questions.question: Which nation reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2002 while co-hosting with Japan?
questions.fun_fact: South Korea beat both Italy and Spain in the knockout rounds on the way to fourth place, their best-ever finish.

questions.question: Which country has lost three World Cup finals without winning any?
questions.fun_fact: 1974, 1978 and 2010. The first two were lost to the host nation.

questions.question: Which nation famously beat England 1-0 at the 1950 World Cup in one of the sport's biggest upsets?
questions.fun_fact: The US side were part-timers including a dishwasher and a postman; some British papers assumed the 1-0 score was a typo for 10-0.

questions.question: Which country has appeared at every single men's World Cup ever held?
questions.fun_fact: Italy and Germany have each missed at least one tournament, but Brazil has played in all of them since 1930.

questions.question: Which four-time champion failed to qualify for the 2018 World Cup entirely?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first time in 60 years Italy missed a World Cup, ending a streak of 14 consecutive appearances.

questions.question: Which Caribbean nation, ranked among the world's lowest, qualified for the 1998 World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Jamaica's 'Reggae Boyz' became the first English-speaking Caribbean nation to reach a World Cup, and beat Japan in the group stage.

questions.question: Which nation reached the 1990 World Cup quarter-finals, sparked by a 38-year-old striker?
questions.fun_fact: Roger Milla came out of retirement to score four goals, and Cameroon beat reigning champions Argentina in the opener despite finishing with nine men.

questions.question: Which nation, with a population under 350,000, became the smallest country ever to qualify for a men's World Cup in 2018?
questions.fun_fact: Iceland's part-time setup once featured a national coach who also worked as a dentist and several players holding ordinary day jobs.

questions.question: In 1966, which team made its only-ever World Cup appearance and stunned Italy to reach the quarter-finals?
questions.fun_fact: North Korea led Portugal 3-0 in the quarter-final before Eusébio scored four goals to turn the match around.

questions.question: At which World Cup was goal-line technology used for the first time?
questions.fun_fact: It arrived after the goal not given to Frank Lampard in 2010, which everyone in the ground could see except the linesman.

questions.question: Which African nation reached the World Cup semi-finals for the first time in history in 2022?
questions.fun_fact: Morocco knocked out both Spain and Portugal, becoming the first African and first Arab nation to reach a men's World Cup semi-final.

questions.question: Which country won the World Cup in both 1934 and 1938?
questions.fun_fact: Only Brazil, in 1958 and 1962, has since managed two in a row.

questions.question: Which nation endured a 32-year gap between World Cup appearances before returning in 2006?
questions.fun_fact: Australia hadn't appeared since 1974; soon afterwards they left Oceania to join the Asian confederation, making qualification far easier.

questions.question: Which country reached its first-ever World Cup final in 2018, beating England in the semi-final?
questions.fun_fact: Croatia played three straight knockout matches that went to extra time, racking up nearly a full extra match before even reaching the final.

questions.question: Which nation was the only team at the 2010 World Cup to finish undefeated, yet still failed to advance?
questions.fun_fact: New Zealand drew all three group games. It led reigning champions Italy through Shane Smeltz in the 7th minute before conceding a penalty, and rescued a point against Slovakia in stoppage time.

questions.question: Which country was awarded a World Cup win by forfeit in 1938 because its opponent simply never showed up?
questions.fun_fact: Austria had been annexed by Germany and ceased to exist as a team, so Sweden advanced without kicking a ball in the round.

questions.question: What happens to the original solid-gold FIFA World Cup trophy that the winning team holds up?

answers.text: The team gives it back; they only keep a replica
The team keeps it forever as a permanent prize
It is melted down and recast after each tournament

questions.fun_fact: Since 1974 the trophy has stayed FIFA property — winners get a gold-plated bronze replica to take home, and the real cup goes straight back into FIFA's possession.

questions.question: There is no room left to engrave new winners on the base of the current World Cup trophy after which year?
questions.fun_fact: The trophy's base has space for only 17 winners' name plates; once 2038 fills the last slot, FIFA will need a redesigned base or a new trophy.

questions.question: Although it looks like a solid gold statuette, what is actually true of the FIFA World Cup trophy's construction?

answers.text: Its upper portion is hollow to keep the weight manageable
It is solid 18-carat gold all the way through
The figures are gold-plated brass, not real gold

questions.fun_fact: The trophy is about 6.1 kg of 18-carat gold — if it were solid all the way through it would weigh roughly 70–80 kg, so the upper portion is hollow.

questions.question: The very first World Cup trophy was once hidden under a bed in a shoebox to keep it safe during World War II. Who hid it there?
questions.fun_fact: Ottorino Barassi smuggled the Jules Rimet trophy out of a bank vault and kept it in a shoebox under his bed in Rome so occupying troops couldn't seize it.

questions.question: Which host nation won the 1978 final after extra time?
questions.fun_fact: It won 3-1 against the Netherlands, who were losing a second final in a row after 1974.

questions.question: The original Jules Rimet trophy was permanently given to Brazil after they won it a third time. What happened to it afterward?

answers.text: It was stolen again in 1983 and never recovered
It is on display in a museum in Rio today
It was returned to FIFA after a legal dispute

questions.fun_fact: Brazil kept it permanently after their 1970 win, but it was stolen from the federation's headquarters in 1983 and is widely believed to have been melted down.

questions.question: For most of World Cup history, who supplied the official match ball?

answers.text: Whichever host nation's manufacturer was chosen
Adidas, from the very first tournament onward
FIFA manufactured the balls itself in Switzerland

questions.fun_fact: Adidas only became the exclusive ball supplier in 1970; before that, host countries supplied balls — and in the 1930 final the two teams even argued over whose ball to use.

questions.question: Which goalkeeper captained his country to the World Cup title in 2010?
questions.fun_fact: He saved a one-on-one from Arjen Robben in the final with his outstretched boot, minutes before Spain scored.

questions.question: The 2010 World Cup ball, the Jabulani, became infamous among players for what reason?

answers.text: It moved unpredictably in the air, frustrating goalkeepers
It was too heavy and caused players' injuries

questions.fun_fact: Its ultra-smooth surface caused erratic 'knuckleball' flight; goalkeepers hated it so much that NASA later studied its aerodynamics to explain the swerve.

questions.question: The 2022 World Cup ball contained something no previous match ball had. What was it?

answers.text: A motion sensor sending data 500 times per second
A built-in GPS tracker for anti-theft
A small camera in the panel seams

questions.fun_fact: The Al Rihla ball held a sensor that helped detect exact kick moments for offside calls — it was central to disallowing a Cristiano Ronaldo 'goal' he claimed to have headed.

questions.question: At the 1986 World Cup, the mascot was a jalapeño pepper. What was its most unusual feature?

answers.text: It had a moustache and sombrero
It could change color in the heat
It was the first mascot with no face

questions.fun_fact: Named 'Pique' (a pun on picante), the chili-pepper mascot leaned hard into Mexican stereotype iconography that would raise eyebrows today.

questions.question: The 1966 England World Cup mascot 'World Cup Willie' is credited as a historical first. What was it?

answers.text: The first official World Cup mascot ever
The first mascot to be an animal
The first mascot voiced by a celebrity

questions.fun_fact: World Cup Willie, a lion in a Union Jack shirt, was the first World Cup mascot — and arguably the first major sporting mascot, predating most Olympic ones.

questions.question: The 2010 World Cup in South Africa was the first tournament where the host's home crowd became famous for what sound?

answers.text: The drone of plastic vuvuzela horns

questions.fun_fact: The vuvuzela's constant 120-decibel hum was so disruptive that broadcasters developed audio filters and some players said they couldn't hear teammates on the pitch.

questions.question: Which referee lost control of the brutal 1962 'Battle of Santiago' between Chile and Italy, an experience that later inspired a famous invention?

answers.text: A FIFA official who abandoned the game early
A local Chilean referee later banned for life

questions.fun_fact: Aston needed police help to get two Italians off the pitch during the chaos — and the experience later inspired him to invent the yellow and red card system after stopping at a traffic light.

questions.question: What everyday object inspired the invention of yellow and red cards in football?

answers.text: Playing cards from a poker game

questions.fun_fact: Referee Ken Aston conceived the cards while stopped at a traffic light — yellow for caution, red for stop — and they debuted at the 1970 World Cup.

questions.question: Which was the first World Cup held outside Europe and South America?
questions.fun_fact: The first eight tournaments alternated between the two continents; Mexico broke the pattern in 1970.

questions.question: Which was the first World Cup contested by 32 teams?
questions.fun_fact: The field had grown from 16 to 24 in 1982 and stayed at 32 until the 2026 expansion to 48.

questions.question: The 'golden goal' rule, where the first goal in extra time ended the match, was used at how many World Cups?

answers.text: Only two tournaments before being scrapped
It is still in use today

questions.fun_fact: Golden goal applied at only two World Cups, 1998 and 2002, and was abolished by 2004 because it made teams play too defensively, fearing one mistake.

questions.question: In the very first World Cup match in 1930, what unusual thing was true of the referee compared to today?

answers.text: Referees wore ordinary jackets and ties, not kit
There was no referee, only the two captains
The referee played as an extra outfield player

questions.fun_fact: Early World Cup referees officiated in formal attire — jackets, long trousers and sometimes ties — and standardized referee uniforms only came much later.

questions.question: Who was the first player ever sent off in a World Cup final?
questions.fun_fact: Argentina's Monzón was dismissed in the 1990 final, and a teammate followed him before the final whistle.

questions.question: What was this stadium in Montevideo built for in 1930?
questions.fun_fact: The Estadio Centenario was not finished when the tournament began — rain had delayed the build, and the opening matches had to be played in smaller grounds around the city.

questions.question: What was the first World Cup trophy called?
questions.fun_fact: Brazil were allowed to keep the trophy for good in 1970, after a third title.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 1950 World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: The 1950 World Cup had no final: instead of a knockout match, a four-team final group decided it. That the last game turned out to be a decider was an accident of the schedule.

questions.question: Who scored the goal that won Uruguay the 1950 World Cup at the Maracanã?
questions.fun_fact: Alcides Ghiggia scored in front of some 200,000 people in Rio. He later said only three people had ever silenced the Maracanã: Frank Sinatra, the Pope and himself.

questions.question: Which country won the first World Cup, in 1930?
questions.fun_fact: Uruguay were hosts and reigning Olympic champions. Because the crossing took weeks by ship, only four European teams entered — France, Belgium, Yugoslavia and Romania.

questions.question: How old was Pelé when he won the World Cup in 1958?
questions.fun_fact: 17 years and 249 days. He scored twice in the final against Sweden and is still the youngest world champion.

questions.question: How many teams took part in the first World Cup in Uruguay in 1930?
questions.fun_fact: 13, and nobody had to qualify — they were invited. Only four European sides made the trip, a two-week crossing by ship.

questions.question: How many spectators watched the deciding match at the Maracanã in 1950?
questions.fun_fact: Around 200,000, still the largest crowd ever at a football match. Brazil lost 2-1 to Uruguay and the stadium fell silent.

questions.question: How many goals were scored in the highest-scoring World Cup match ever, Austria against Switzerland in 1954?
questions.fun_fact: 7-5 to Austria, in 40-degree heat in Lausanne. The Austrian goalkeeper suffered heatstroke and afterwards had no memory of playing.

questions.question: After how many seconds was the fastest goal in World Cup history scored?
questions.fun_fact: Eleven seconds, by Hakan Şükür in the 2002 third-place match. It was his only goal of the tournament.

questions.question: The 1994 final between Brazil and Italy made World Cup history in which way?

answers.text: First final refereed by a woman
First final replayed a week later

questions.fun_fact: After 120 goalless minutes Roberto Baggio, Italy's biggest star, blazed the decisive penalty over the bar in the heat of Pasadena.

questions.question: In 2010, which animal 'predicted' the winner of all of Germany's matches and the final correctly?
questions.fun_fact: Paul the Octopus lived in an aquarium in Oberhausen and picked from two food boxes marked with flags — he went eight for eight, including Spain's win in the final.

questions.question: What was unusual about when the 2022 World Cup in Qatar was played?
questions.fun_fact: The summer heat in Qatar forced the move, so European leagues paused mid-season — the first World Cup not played in May, June or July.

questions.question: Stadium 974 at the 2022 World Cup was built largely out of what?
questions.fun_fact: It used 974 containers — also Qatar's international dialling code — and was designed to be taken apart after the tournament, a first for a World Cup venue.

questions.question: Which refereeing aid was used at a men's World Cup for the first time in 2018?
questions.fun_fact: VAR helped award a record number of penalties in Russia, including one in the final that Antoine Griezmann converted for France.

questions.question: Naranjito, the mascot of the 1982 World Cup in Spain, was what?
questions.fun_fact: The name means 'little orange', a nod to Spain's famous citrus groves — he even got his own animated TV series.

questions.question: Germany's 2006 mascot, Goleo VI the lion, drew mockery for missing what?
questions.fun_fact: Goleo wore only a Germany shirt, and his sidekick was a talking football called Pille — the toy company that held the licence went insolvent that same year.

questions.question: Fuleco, the mascot of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, was which animal?
questions.fun_fact: The three-banded armadillo can roll itself into a ball — and it is a threatened species, which the mascot was meant to highlight.

questions.question: What went wrong for singer Diana Ross at the opening ceremony of the 1994 World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: She shot wide from just a few yards out — and the goal was rigged to split open anyway, as if she had scored.

questions.question: Why is the stadium crowd 'wave' called the Mexican wave in much of the world?

answers.text: TV beamed it worldwide from Mexico 1986
It copies a traditional Mexican dance
Mexico's 1970 team celebrated goals that way

questions.fun_fact: Fans in North America had been doing the wave since the early 1980s, but viewers elsewhere first saw it on TV from the 1986 World Cup, and the name stuck.

questions.question: Why did England's Paul Gascoigne burst into tears during the 1990 semi-final?

answers.text: A yellow card meant he'd miss the final

questions.fun_fact: England lost the shootout to West Germany anyway, but the image of 'Gazza' in tears helped make him a national hero.

questions.question: Before every match at the 1998 World Cup, French defender Laurent Blanc kissed what for luck?
questions.fun_fact: Blanc was sent off in the semi-final and missed the final itself, but France still won the title on home soil.

questions.question: Luis Suárez was sent home from the 2014 World Cup for what?
questions.fun_fact: Italy's Giorgio Chiellini was the victim — it was the third time Suárez had been punished for biting an opponent.

questions.question: Frank Rijkaard and Rudi Völler were both sent off in a 1990 match after an incident involving what?
questions.fun_fact: Rijkaard spat at Völler twice; both were dismissed, and the pair later made up and filmed a butter commercial together.

questions.question: What did Brandi Chastain do after scoring the winning penalty in the 1999 Women's World Cup final?
questions.fun_fact: The final between the USA and China drew over 90,000 fans to the Rose Bowl, one of the biggest crowds ever for a women's sports event.

questions.question: The 1970 World Cup ball, the Telstar, had black and white panels for what reason?

answers.text: To show up better on black-and-white TV
To copy the host's national colours

questions.fun_fact: The name came from the Telstar communications satellite, and its 32-panel design became the classic image of a football.

questions.question: What did referees use at a World Cup for the first time in 2014 to mark where a wall must stand?
questions.fun_fact: The foam disappears within about a minute, and it had already been used in South American football before FIFA adopted it.

questions.question: What colour shirts did England wear when they won the 1966 World Cup final?
questions.fun_fact: Both teams normally played in white, so England changed into their red second kit while West Germany kept white shirts with black shorts.

questions.question: Brazil's Rivaldo was fined at the 2002 World Cup after he did what against Turkey?

answers.text: Clutched his face after being hit on the leg
Kicked the ball into the crowd

questions.fun_fact: The ball struck his thigh, but he went down holding his face and got a Turkish player sent off — Brazil went on to win the whole tournament.

questions.question: When a stray dog ran onto the pitch during Brazil v England in 1962, what happened to Jimmy Greaves after he caught it?

answers.text: It ran off with his boot

questions.fun_fact: There were no spare shirts, so Greaves played on in the soiled one. The dog was later raffled among Brazil's squad, and Garrincha won it.

questions.question: How long did matches last at the first Women's World Cup in 1991?
questions.fun_fact: Officials doubted women could play a full 90 minutes, so halves lasted 40 — from 1995 matches ran the standard length.

questions.question: The official title of the first Women's World Cup in 1991 included the name of which sponsor?
questions.fun_fact: FIFA was reluctant to lend the 'World Cup' brand, so it was called the FIFA World Championship for Women's Football for the M&M's Cup. China hosted, and the USA won.

questions.question: Why was the 2003 Women's World Cup moved from China to the USA?

answers.text: An outbreak of the SARS virus
China withdrew for lack of stadiums

questions.fun_fact: The switch came only four months before kick-off. China got the 2007 edition instead.

questions.question: When Japan won the 2011 Women's World Cup, it became the first team from which continent to win a senior World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Japan came from behind twice against the USA in the final, including a goal in the 117th minute, before winning the shootout.

questions.question: Which was the first country to win both the men's and the women's World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Germany's women won in 2003 and again in 2007, and Spain became the second country to complete the double in 2023.

questions.question: By what score did the USA beat Thailand at the 2019 Women's World Cup?
questions.fun_fact: Alex Morgan scored five goals, and the USA faced criticism for celebrating each goal right up to the last one.

questions.question: Germany's women won the 2007 World Cup with which remarkable record?

answers.text: They didn't concede a single goal
They won every match on penalties

questions.fun_fact: Goalkeeper Nadine Angerer even saved a penalty from Brazil's Marta in the final, which Germany won 2–0.

questions.question: Before the 1970 World Cup, England captain Bobby Moore was arrested in Colombia accused of stealing what?
questions.fun_fact: He was held for days in Bogotá before the case collapsed, then flew on to Mexico and played superbly all tournament.

questions.question: What did FIFA demand of the USA in return for hosting the 1994 World Cup?

answers.text: Put soccer in all public schools

questions.fun_fact: The promise became Major League Soccer, which kicked off in 1996.

questions.question: What was unique about the 1994 World Cup match between the USA and Switzerland at the Pontiac Silverdome?

answers.text: It was the first World Cup game played indoors
It was played on artificial turf

questions.fun_fact: Grass was grown in hexagonal trays outside and wheeled into the domed stadium, and the teams drew 1–1.

questions.question: What happened to South Korea's Ahn Jung-hwan after his golden goal knocked Italy out of the 2002 World Cup?

answers.text: His Italian club's owner vowed to sack him
He was banned from playing in Italy

questions.fun_fact: Perugia's owner said he would not pay a player who had 'ruined Italian football'. Ahn never played for the club again.

questions.question: Spain won the 2010 World Cup despite losing their opening match. Who beat them?
questions.fun_fact: Spain were the first team to lose their opening game and still win the title, and Argentina did the same in 2022 after losing to Saudi Arabia.

questions.question: In the 2014 semi-final, Germany led hosts Brazil by how much at half-time?
questions.fun_fact: Four of the goals came in just six minutes, and the match finished 7–1, a result Brazilians call the 'Mineirazo'.

questions.question: What did Dutch coach Louis van Gaal do just before the penalty shootout against Costa Rica in 2014?

answers.text: Let his players pick the takers by lot

questions.fun_fact: Substitute Tim Krul had been sent on only for the shootout, and he saved two penalties to send the Netherlands through.

questions.question: How did Japan get past Senegal at the 2018 World Cup when both finished level on points, goals and head-to-head?

answers.text: They won a drawing of lots

questions.fun_fact: It was the first time the 'fair play' tiebreaker decided anything at a World Cup: Japan had four yellow cards, Senegal six.

questions.question: What made French referee Stéphanie Frappart famous at the 2022 World Cup?

answers.text: First woman to referee a men's World Cup match
First referee to show a red card via VAR

questions.fun_fact: She took charge of Costa Rica against Germany, with women as both assistant referees too.

questions.question: Why did the 1982 match between France and Kuwait stop for several minutes after a French goal?

answers.text: A Kuwaiti sheikh marched onto the pitch

questions.fun_fact: Kuwait's players had stopped when they heard a whistle from the crowd. Sheikh Fahad came down from the stands, and the goal was actually disallowed.

questions.question: What happened in the only World Cup meeting between West Germany and East Germany, in 1974?

answers.text: It ended in a goalless draw

questions.fun_fact: Jürgen Sparwasser scored the winner in Hamburg, yet West Germany went on to win the tournament anyway.

questions.question: After Brazil's shock loss at home in 1950, how was the new yellow national kit chosen?

answers.text: Through a vote by the players

questions.fun_fact: The winner, Aldyr Schlee, was a 19-year-old illustrator from the border with Uruguay — the very team that had beaten Brazil.

questions.question: What did Iran's players hand their opponents before their politically charged match against the USA in 1998?
questions.fun_fact: The teams posed together for a joint photo before kick-off. Iran won 2–1.

questions.question: Which World Cup host is the only one ever required to play a qualifier to get into its own tournament?
questions.fun_fact: 1934 was the first World Cup with qualifying at all, and Italy beat Greece 4–0 in a one-off game — before going on to win the title.

questions.question: The linesman who allowed Geoff Hurst's famous 1966 final goal has a national stadium named after him. In which country?
questions.fun_fact: Tofiq Bahramov was often called 'the Russian linesman' in England, but he came from Baku, where the national stadium bears his name.

questions.question: Why did France play Hungary at the 1978 World Cup in green-and-white striped shirts?

answers.text: Both teams had brought white kits
In protest at the Argentine regime

questions.fun_fact: The shirts were borrowed from Kimberley, a local club in Mar del Plata, and the kick-off was delayed by about 40 minutes.

questions.question: At the 1974 World Cup, Haiti's Emmanuel Sanon scored against Italy and ended what?

answers.text: Dino Zoff's run of 1,142 minutes without conceding
Italy's streak of 12 straight clean sheets at World Cups

questions.fun_fact: The goal silenced Italy's fans, but Italy still came back to win 3–1.

questions.question: How did Wales qualify for the 1958 World Cup after finishing second in their group?

answers.text: As a replacement for a banned team
Through a later appeal to FIFA

questions.fun_fact: Israel's opponents had all refused to play them, and FIFA wouldn't let a team qualify without a match. Wales were drawn out of the runners-up and beat Israel 2–0 twice.

questions.question: Brazilian midfielder Formiga played at how many Women's World Cups?
questions.fun_fact: Her tournaments ran from 1995 to 2019, and she was 41 when she played at the last one in France.

questions.question: Garrincha was sent off in Brazil's 1962 semi-final. What happened next?

answers.text: The ban was lifted and he played the final
Brazil won the final without him
He was replaced by a teenage Pelé

questions.fun_fact: He was the tournament's star after Pelé got injured, and Brazil beat Czechoslovakia 3–1 to defend their title.

questions.question: Which team became the first from Asia to play at a World Cup, in 1938?
questions.fun_fact: The team from today's Indonesia played only one match, losing 6–0 to Hungary, and went straight home.

questions.question: Why did Scotland skip the 1950 World Cup even though they had earned a place?

answers.text: They'd vowed to go only as British champions
They couldn't afford the trip to Brazil

questions.fun_fact: The British Home Championship doubled as a qualifying group with two places. Scotland finished second behind England and stayed home.

questions.question: How many players were sent off in the 2006 'Battle of Nuremberg' between Portugal and the Netherlands?
questions.fun_fact: Russian referee Valentin Ivanov also showed 16 yellow cards, and Portugal won 1–0.
